explainer_content.short_definition: 2000s radio pop with club propulsion, R&B crossover muscle, and high-gloss producer architecture.
explainer_content.history_capsule: Beyonce, Rihanna, Lady Gaga, and peers made the 2000s pop center feel rhythmic, electronic, and globally club-aware without leaving the Top 40 frame.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It shows how dancefloor language moved from scene context into default pop grammar.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: Unlike 1990s teen pop, the engine is the groove and the producer texture as much as the star image.
